author: julie
content: JOBBER COMMUNITY TEAM "What's your 2026 Business Goal?" How to enter: Register for Jobber Summit 2026. Attend either the morning or evening event on March 4. Bonus entries (2): to this giveaway thread and tell us about your business goals for 2026. What are you hoping to grow, improve, or finally prioritize this year? Engage elsewhere in the forum Leave a on another member’s post or create your own post outside of this giveaway post. replies.content: NEW MEMBER Thanks to jobber I was able to scale my business within the first month , landed a 50 k landscape job, the professionalism of being able to send a quote , jobber pay ,feature kicks in ! Everything about jobber is amazing exited for the summit looking forward to growing MattCafaro NEW MEMBER 3 hours ago I started my company as a side biz 4 years ago sence last year to now my business has grown exponentially and I'm hoping that I can triple my income and this will be last last year doing my business as a side biz and I can hire 2 more guys by the end of this year. LonestarCI NEW MEMBER 6 hours ago Our 2026 business goal at Lonestar Construction Industries is simple and deeply rooted in who we are: expand our reach while staying true to the down‑to‑earth Texas values that built this company. This year, we’re focused on growing our audience, strengthening our presence through new memberships, and opening more doors for meaningful partnerships. But more than anything, we’re doubling down on what has always fueled our success — genuine relationships and word‑of‑mouth referrals from people who know our work and know our heart. Those who’ve worked with us, or know our CEO, understand that Lonestar isn’t just another construction company. We’re neighbors serving neighbors, committed to quality, honesty, and making a real difference in our communities. As Relationship Manager and Lead Generator, I’m excited to help us reach more families, more businesses, and more partners who value craftsmanship and connection. 2026 is about growth, yes — but growth rooted in trust, reputation, and the people who believe in us. CasaMontana_406 NEW MEMBER 7 hours ago We are a residential housekeeping company in Montana. This first year has been tough since we didn't expect the business to take off as fast as it did and we weren't prepared. This year we are looking to use Jobber and 2 other tools all integrated together to help us with CRM, marketing, dispatch, bookkeeping, and mostly organization and automation so that we can run much smoother this year than last year. We have a high goal to achieve 300% of the revenue in 2026 as we did in 2025. We're looking forward to learning, learning, and learning some more from the Jobber Summit, other webinars/seminars, and most importantly other business owners in the (online) community. CraigRenfro NEW MEMBER 1 day ago I started my business when I was 14 years old. I am 19 now and am looking to expand my business in 2026 by adding a mowing crew and a landscaping crew. I hope this is doable but am thankful for where I am now. I want to keep quality and professionalism as the main focus of my company though, so I don’t want to grow to fast. 21Handyman NEW MEMBER 1 day ago Go from myself (one) to 6 handymen in the area and begin expanding to the next region. Systematizing operations to eliminate redundancies, waste and focusing on smooth operations for the operator and customer. And find a mentor for guidance along the way to not recreate the wheel, as it were. Alex_NCM 2 days ago We are residential and commercial cleaning company. In 2026, my goal is to grow a more stable and profitable cleaning business by focusing on reliable recurring clients and stronger systems. I want to increase recurring clients and predictable revenue, strengthen systems and reduce daily firefighting dielectra 2 days ago In 2026, we are looking to tighten our routes and possibly start a third route for our lawncare business. Also looking more to reporting to understand how to more efficiently run our business. NinjaScoopz 3 days ago As we wrap up our first year in business, growth is very much on our radar. We’ve scooped for 20+ clients so far, a few one-off cleanups and mostly repeat visits. Our big goal is to hit 50 regular clients by summer 2026. Ambitious? Sure. Doable? Absolutely. Also, tell your dog. Laura1111 4 days ago From NJ - Our goal for 2026 is to transition from traditional road service and gas station inventory work for a company into an independent, hands-on service business that can grow from weekends into a full-time livelihood. My husband currently works in road service and inventory at a gas station. He’s highly skilled with physical, practical work and wants to build something of his own rather than stay in a job that relies heavily on long hours and overtime. We plan to start the business on weekends, use that income to first replace his overtime, and then steadily grow it to replace his full-time job which totals $50k a year with OT and commissions. This year, we’re focused on: - Discovering which type of business to do that can help turning his existing hands-on experience into a customer-facing service business - Validating demand with weekend jobs and repeat customers - Learning how to price services correctly and build simple systems early (scheduling, invoicing, communication) - Creating a clear, realistic path from side hustle to full-time work By the end of 2026, our goal is to have consistent weekend and/or evening work, steady referrals, and a strong foundation to make the transition into full-time self-employment.
